newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Northrop says hopeful of NATO contract.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Northrop says hopeful of NATO contract.

text.p: Defence manufacturer Northrop Grumman Corp said on Wednesday it remained hopeful that the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) would select its Joint-STARS aircraft to meet the alliance's air-to-ground surveillance needs.
"The NATO alliance has expressed interest in the Joint-STARS system," Northrop Grumman International president William James told Reuters.
The Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System (Joint-STARS) uses Boeing Co 707s aircraft.
The aircraft are fitted with a powerful surveillance and target acquisition radar system to distinguish moving or fixed targets from other types of objects on the ground.

James, who is visiting Australia for an air show featuring a number of international defence contractors, said a contract with NATO would see Northrop supply between six and 12 Joint-STARS aircraft worth about US$225 million each.

"This year (NATO) will deliberate and we hope will decide on whether or not they are going to purchase the Joint-STARS system. That'll probably result in a study contract and then a firm contract in 1998, I believe," he said.
Deliveries would probably start in 2000 or 2001 if a deal was struck, James said.
U.S. President Bill Clinton said last October he would tout the Joint-STARS system to NATO.
The United States Defense Department has agreed to buy 19 for the U.S. Air Force at a cost of about US$9 billion. Northrop has supplied the U.S. with two so far.
James said the system had already proven itself during the Bosnia and Desert Storm conflicts.
"It's proven itself as a worthy air-to-ground system," he said.
James said Joint-STARS had little competition as it was more sophisticated than helicopter-based solutions offered by France and Italy. Britain also as a system on the drawing board.
"Right now and probably for a number of years there will not be any competition at the level of capability and sophistication that the Joint-STARS is at right at the moment," he said.
